headline: BARRICK BEATS Q1 ESTIMATES: 1.05M oz at ~$1,250 AISC against $4,878 gold — margins above $3,600/oz
snippet: Barrick Mining released Q1 2026 results this morning — 1.05 million gold-equivalent ounces at ~$1,250/oz AISC against gold averaging near $4,878/oz, implying per-ounce margins above $3,600. Analysts had forecast $0.74 EPS on $4.53B revenue, a year-over-year EPS increase of more than 111%; the stock had already climbed 7% in the weeks leading into the print.

headline: ANGLOGOLD POSTS RECORD $1.2B FREE CASH FLOW, launches $2B buyback — dividend surges 830% YoY to $1.16/share
snippet: AngloGold Ashanti's Q1 2026 free cash flow of $1.2B was nearly triple the prior-year Q1 figure, while EBITDA surged 130% to $2.29B on 724,000oz produced. The board approved a $2B share buyback and declared an interim dividend of $1.16/share — up from $0.125 a year ago — as the miner swings from $755M net debt to $868M net cash.

headline: UR-ENERGY Q1 URANIUM PRODUCTION +48% YoY: Shirley Basin ISR facility commissioned, second mine now online
snippet: Ur-Energy (NASDAQ: URG) captured 110,314 lbs U₃O₈ in Q1 2026 — up 48% year-over-year — at a cash cost of $37.51/lb and a realized sales price of $70.98/lb. Its second ISR mining facility at Shirley Basin, Wyoming, commenced operations in April 2026, with first uranium shipments expected this summer pending final regulatory approval.

headline: SAN LORENZO HITS ALL-TIME HIGH: 102.3 metres @ 1.33 g/t gold in 3.9km step-out expands Chile porphyry
snippet: San Lorenzo Gold (TSXV: SLG) released holes SAL-09 and SAL-10 at the Arco de Oro target on the Salvadora project in Chile's mega-porphyry belt — including 102.3m @ 1.33 g/t gold and 59m @ 1.07 g/t, both 3.9km beyond any prior drilling. VP of Exploration says the results indicate 'a much larger system than earlier thought,' sending shares to a record.

headline: SILVER47 PULLS 1,713 G/T SILVER AND 38.7 G/T GOLD from 15km Nevada vein network barely touched by drill
snippet: Silver47 Exploration (TSXV: AGA) reported rock-sample assays from its Kennedy Gold-Silver Project in Nevada — up to 1,713 g/t silver and 38.7 g/t gold — across a 15km vein network that remains largely undrilled. The company is simultaneously running a 7,000m drill program at its Tonopah-adjacent Hughes Project and holds ~$54M in working capital.

headline: ADAMERA STAKES THIRD TUNGSTEN PROPERTY in Washington State as U.S. military demand forecast up 12% in 2026
snippet: Adamera Minerals (TSXV: ADZ) staked the Pierre Creek Tungsten property in Washington State — 14km east of its Talisman Tungsten Project — securing a scheelite-bearing skarn deposit as the U.S. Defense Industrial Base Consortium actively solicits domestic tungsten supply proposals. Military application tungsten demand is projected to grow 12% in 2026.

headline: LUMINA METALS IN KGHM COPPER TALKS after closing C$406M Toronto IPO — Poland's 604Mt Cu-Ag resource in play
snippet: Lumina Metals (TSX: LMCU) — which closed Canada's largest mining IPO since 2021 at C$406.2M — has opened copper concentrate supply talks with state miner KGHM targeting offtake from its Nowa Sól deposit in Poland (604Mt @ 1.24% Cu, 38 g/t Ag). The company listed April 30 and traded flat on debut; KGHM discussions are the first major commercial step post-IPO.

headline: CHILE LITHIUM EXPORTS SURGE 175%: SQM-Codelco ramp delivers $498M in April as Q1 volume climbs 25%
snippet: Chile's April mining exports totalled $5.96B with lithium carbonate up 175.6% YoY to $498M, driven by the SQM-Codelco partnership accelerating production in 2026. Q1 lithium shipments rose 25% by volume with $1.1B in revenue (+148% YoY), positioning Chile to challenge Chinese producers as the SQM-Codelco joint venture scales toward full capacity.

headline: NDPR DROPS 21% IN APRIL to $99/kg — still 88% above January lows; Western producers remain profitable
snippet: NdPr oxide pulled back sharply to $99.61/kg in April — the sharpest monthly decline since the Q1 rally began — but remains well above the cost floor for MP Materials and Lynas. The May 2026 outlook notes the U.S. $12B Project Vault Strategic Critical Minerals Reserve and ongoing government support programs underpin long-term Western rare earth supply chain buildout.

headline: GOLD IS DECOUPLING FROM GEOPOLITICS — and the data proves it: peace rallies, war selloffs since January
snippet: GoldSilver.com examines why gold has sold off on every Iran war escalation and rallied on every peace signal in 2026 — the opposite of the traditional war-premium playbook. The thesis: with U.S. gross federal debt above 125% of GDP, markets need lower oil, lower inflation, and lower interest rates, and only peace delivers that chain reaction.
